title: Constructing simple geometrical figures
summary: Plan and verify constructions using rulers, compasses, set squares and protractors.
objectives: Choose suitable instruments and data for a geometric construction.
Construct and verify angle bisectors, perpendicular bisectors and parallel lines.
Construct triangles from SSS, SAS or ASA data and check that the data determine the figure.

blocks.text: SSS uses three side lengths, SAS uses two sides and their included angle, and ASA uses two angles and the included side. Equal-radius arcs construct perpendicular bisectors and angle bisectors; copied corresponding angles construct parallel lines.

Straightedge-and-compass construction preserves exact geometric conditions. Equal-radius arcs from the endpoints of a segment locate points equidistant from both endpoints; joining the arc intersections gives the perpendicular bisector. Equal arcs from the sides of an angle locate its angle bisector.

Keep construction arcs visible because they are the evidence. For SSS, draw one side and intersect two circles. For SAS, construct the included angle between the two known sides. For ASA, construct the two known angles at the ends of the known side. Verify lengths and angles after construction.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: A 92° angle is bisected. Find either constructed angle.

sections.verification_note: The result follows the stated property and satisfies the original geometric conditions.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: Construct triangle ABC with AB=7 cm, AC=5 cm and BC=4 cm, then describe why the construction is unique up to reflection.

content.text: With centre A and radius 5 cm draw an arc. With centre B and radius 4 cm draw a second arc.
Label an intersection C and join AC and BC. The two possible intersections are mirror images across AB.

sections.verification_note: Measure AC and BC and keep both intersecting arcs visible as evidence of the SSS construction.

blocks.text: Do not erase the arcs used to locate a point. A ruler with no compass construction does not demonstrate an exact bisector. Check that two arcs actually intersect; otherwise the proposed triangle data may be impossible.

prompt.text: A perpendicular bisector crosses a 12 cm segment. How far is the crossing from an endpoint?

feedback.text: The crossing is the midpoint, 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

blocks.text: Name the relevant property, write the complete angle or construction relationship, calculate carefully, and check that every angle and length is geometrically possible.
Before moving on, explain the relevant property in words, show the equation or formula with units, and use the diagram markings to check that every correspondence is consistent.
